name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs—open and merged—for two weeks. This gives us full visibility into how PR-Agent behaves across the entire lifecycle, catching edge cases that only appear after merging. The trade-off is higher resource usage, but the data is worth it to avoid surprises later.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode trains reviewers to dismiss *all* autofeedback as noise, not just the false positives—once that habit forms, real issues get ignored too. Instead, run PR-Agent only on high-risk PRs (e.g., changes touching core logic or dependencies) for a week, then measure if the signal-to-noise ratio justifies expanding. Settle it by comparing reviewer engagement metrics before/after the trial—if engagement drops, the experiment fails.
